analysis:
Documentation-only units were reviewed. In docs/operations/provider-release.md, head lines 1033-1039 add guidance that release deactivation stops only new installs. They point operators to `darkbloom update --rollback`, which restores the retained predecessor locally, quarantines the bad release, contacts no coordinator and leaves auto-update on. In docs/provider/cli-reference.md, the patch (head lines 743-769 and 1852-1860) documents the --rollback and --yes flags. It also documents these claimed behaviors: mutual exclusion with --check-only, --override-quarantine and --coordinator; drain through the watchdog's journaled rollback under the update lease; refusal in cluster pairs, foreground providers or lease contention; and refusal when the kept release fails its hash or signature check. The --override-quarantine description widens to cover releases rolled back with --rollback.

Security relevance (T-043, T-013, T-034, T-054, A-011, A-017, TB-003): local rollback runs on the operator-controlled Mac. The coordinator's release/qualification policy, not local state, decides serving authorization. A rolled-back older build still needs current qualification and must not be revoked (provider-release.md 1041-1045). Docs alone add no new attack surface beyond operator-local actions that ADV-001 already controls. The implementation of UpdateRollback.swift and SelfUpdater+Rollback.swift is not supplied, so the hash/signature verification of the retained predecessor, the lease and journal semantics, and the quarantine handling cannot be verified here. Integration should check those against the T-043 watchdog rollback authority. A threat-model note may be warranted: T-043 describes automatic predecessor rollback, and an operator-initiated rollback path now exists. It should also be confirmed that coordinator policy rejects rolled-back builds whose qualification is revoked. Base cli-reference lines 1-385 are unchanged context. No regression was identified from the documentation.
